title: Technician Efficiency shows the exact percentage and equals its report
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in a fresh test location made for this run, so nothing else is invoiced, credited or clocked there; on the Dashboard, the Technician Efficiency tile on This Week shows no percentage (a grey "-").
  3. You run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week.
  4. A test customer with one contact and one asset that uses that contact (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer 1, contact Dana Test, unit ZZ-101).
  5. Technician 1 is you (Admin ShopView, Time Clock on): in a fresh location you are the technician offered in Add Technician, and you clock time yourself.
  6. Advisor A: you (Admin ShopView); the Service Advisor in the work order's left panel shows your name by default.
  7. One invoiced work order (not sent, not paid), Service Advisor Advisor A, two labor lines for Technician 1 at $100.00 an hour whose Tech Time differs from Estimated Time: ZZAUTOTEST Line 1 (Estimated Time 2.00, Tech Time 1.80) and ZZAUTOTEST Line 2 (Estimated Time 1.50, Tech Time 1.20), with exactly 2.00 hours clocked on each line.
custom_steps:
1. Work out Technician Efficiency by hand: invoiced technician hours / clocked hours x 100 = (1.80 + 1.20) / (2.00 + 2.00) x 100 = 3.00 / 4.00 x 100 = 75.00%.
  2. Click Dashboard in the top menu.
  3. On the Technician Efficiency tile click the range pill and choose This Week.
  4. Write down the percentage and the line under it.
  5. Click the arrow icon beside "Technician Efficiency" on the tile (its tooltip names the report).
  6. On the Technician Efficiency report click the Invoiced tab and make sure the Date control shows This week.
  7. Write down Technician 1's Clocked Hrs, Invoiced Tech Hrs and Efficiency.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The tile reads 75.00%, to two decimal places (3.00 / 4.00 x 100).
  • The line under it reads "3.00 Invoiced Tech Hrs / 4.00 Clocked". It uses Tech Time (1.80 + 1.20), not Estimated Time (2.00 + 1.50).
  • On the report's Invoiced tab, Technician 1 shows Clocked Hrs 4.00, Invoiced Tech Hrs 3.00 (the report may print it as 3) and Efficiency 75.00%, the same as the tile.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3), story SV-9576 (S4); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S3 (S3-R1, S3-R2 Technician Efficiency row, context note), S4 (S4-R6, S4-R7). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 06_TechEff_After, 12_technician-efficiency_After (Invoiced / Completed tabs).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R2: “Each measure is calculated as defined in the table below.”
  • S3-R2 table row (Technician Efficiency): “| Technician Efficiency | Invoiced technician hours divided by clocked hours, times 100, for the selected range. Each work order line's technician time is split across the technicians who worked it, in proportion to each technician's share of the clocked time on that line. | Technician Efficiency report (Invoiced) |”
  • S4-R6: “The Technician Efficiency tile headline is the technician efficiency percentage for the selected range, shown to two decimal places.”
  • S4-R7: “The Technician Efficiency tile shows a supporting line reading "{invoiced tech hours} Invoiced Tech Hrs / {clocked hours} Clocked".”
  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”
  • S3 context note (parity check): “to check parity on a KPI tile that shows a shop-wide figure, compare it against the matching report with all advisors or all technicians selected (no filter applied).”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
